critical_code_review_comments: ai_mentor_api.py chat(): For each new message the entire history is replayed by calling chat_instance.send_message in a for-loop (lines 92-95). This issues N extra LLM calls per request and will become extremely slow and expensive as a session grows. Refactor to pass history as system context or use LlmChat's native history support, not re-send_message per turn.

ai_mentor_api.py chat(): Bare except catches all errors and returns a friendly string with HTTP 200 — this hides real failures (network, key invalid, rate-limit). Distinguish transient vs config errors and return proper 5xx where appropriate, or at least include an error flag in the response so the UI can show retry.
questions_api.py: ObjectId(question_id) is called without try/except — passing a malformed id (e.g. random string) will raise bson.errors.InvalidId and bubble up as 500. Wrap and return 400/404.
questions_api.py /admin/upload-image: file.filename used directly to derive extension with no MIME/type validation and no size limit — admin-only but still risky; sanitize.

questions_api.py: routes /admin/* and /{question_id} share the same prefix — FastAPI matches in declaration order which is fine here, but /admin/stats etc could be shadowed if /{question_id} were declared first. Current ordering is correct; add a guard or move /{question_id} to /public/{id} to avoid future regressions.
ai_mentor_api.py: SYSTEM_PROMPT hard-coded in the module — fine for MVP but consider moving to config so non-engineers can iterate.

rca of the issue: AI Mentor Enter-to-send: The chat input element accepts text but pressing Enter does not trigger submission — most likely the input is not wrapped in a <form> with onSubmit, or there is no onKeyDown handler in AIMentor.js. Reproduce: login, open Dashboard > AI Mentor tab, type a question, press Enter. Expected: message sent and assistant reply rendered within ~10s. Actual: input cleared/unchanged, empty state persists. Mitigation: add either (a) <form onSubmit={sendMessage}> around the input row, or (b) onKeyDown={e => e.key==='Enter' && !e.shiftKey && sendMessage()} on the input.
